findings.claim: North Campus was the designated production kitchen in the historical tender.
The authority described about 99.7% of historical tender volume as central-kitchen production distributed to six Istanbul campuses, with tiny remote-unit demand handled separately.
Historical listed quantities were 735,000 student breakfasts, 3,465,000 student meals and 476,500 staff meals.
Historical capacity requirements used 5,000 meals and 500 breakfasts as half of daily requirements.
Historical documents included backup-kitchen continuity requirements tied to serious contract non-compliance risk.
Historical main-course service offered meat and vegan alternatives within total meal quantity.
Selectable meal ratios were economically material enough to be challenged by a bidder.
A 14-day example menu and raw-input gram quantities were part of tender cost formation.
Historical contract penalties could be deducted from contractor payments.
North Campus kitchen renovation temporarily changed production origin at the start of the historical service period.
